skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Reviews code for security vulnerabilities, quality problems, performance risks, testing gaps, and documentation issues using structured guidance and optional local analyzers.
skill.summary: Produce prioritized, evidence-based code review feedback across security, quality, performance, testing, and documentation.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

content.user_title: Review Code for Security, Quality, and Performance
content.value_statement: Manual reviews can miss security, quality, and performance issues. This skill applies a structured workflow and optional analysis tools to produce prioritized feedback.
actual_capabilities: Reviews input validation, authentication, authorization, data exposure, injection, deserialization, and cryptographic risks.
Evaluates complexity, modularity, naming, error handling, duplication, and maintainability.
Identifies inefficient algorithms, database queries, network calls, caching gaps, and resource management problems.
Assesses test coverage, test quality, documentation completeness, and deployment readiness.
Invokes installed Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety tools through the optional Python helper.
Generates Markdown or JSON reports and can write reports to a user-selected path.
limitations: Automated checks require Python and separately installed analysis tools.
The helper primarily automates Python analysis, while guidance for other languages remains manual.
The skill cannot verify business requirements, runtime behavior, or production configuration without relevant context.
Suggested thresholds are general guidance and may not match every project policy.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Prioritize correctness, security, tests, maintainability, and actionable feedback before approval.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers and pull request reviewers

use_cases.title: Prepare a release audit
use_cases.description: Check a codebase for high-impact security, performance, dependency, and deployment risks.

use_cases.title: Build review standards
use_cases.description: Adapt the included workflow and checklist into consistent team review criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Quick code review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [file or change]. List correctness, security, and maintainability issues by severity. Explain each issue and suggest a specific fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused review of a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Security-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [code or directory] for injection, access control, secret exposure, unsafe deserialization, and weak cryptography. Cite evidence and recommend mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Pull request assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [pull request] against its stated goals. Evaluate architecture, performance, tests, documentation, compatibility, and security. Separate blockers from improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a complete pull request decision.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced risk review
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat-model [change], inspect trust boundaries and failure modes, then assess complexity and performance. Rank findings by impact, exploitability, confidence, and remediation effort.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for high-risk systems or release gates.

output_examples.input: Review a login handler that builds a database query from request fields.
output: Critical: User input reaches the query without parameterization, enabling SQL injection.
Fix: Use bound parameters and add tests with malicious input.

output_examples.input: Review a data-processing function with nested loops and no edge-case tests.
output: High: Repeated linear searches create quadratic runtime for large inputs.
Medium: Empty and duplicate inputs lack test coverage.

output_examples.input: Review a small documentation-only pull request.
output_examples.output: No blocking issues found. Verify referenced commands and links during continuous integration.

best_practices: Provide the change goals, affected files, runtime constraints, and project standards.
Ask for file and line evidence with clear severity and confidence.
Run relevant tests and analyzers, then verify important findings manually.
anti_patterns: Do not request a broad review without defining scope or expected behavior.
Do not treat automated scanner output as proof without checking code context.
Do not prioritize formatting feedback above correctness, security, or data integrity.

faq.question: Which languages can this skill review?
faq.answer: The workflow applies broadly, with specific guidance for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Go.

faq.question: Does the helper install analysis tools?
faq.answer: No. Install Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety separately before using the related checks.

faq.question: Can it review an entire repository?
faq.answer: Yes, but focused changes and clear project context usually produce more precise findings.

faq.question: Does it modify reviewed source code?
faq.answer: No. The helper analyzes targets and only writes a report when an output path is supplied.

faq.question: Can it replace human approval?
faq.answer: No. A reviewer must validate findings, business logic, architecture decisions, and release risk.

faq.question: What report formats are available?
faq.answer: The helper exposes Markdown summaries and JSON output through its command-line report options.
